masthead.intro: These terms and ideas are fragments—drawn from scattered disciplines, biased, partial, and reinterpreted through a subjective lens. Scientific concepts are digested and displaced rather than used with strict accuracy. Some parts are inspired by—or shamelessly stolen from—my closest friend ;) This is neither linear storytelling nor an attempt to construct a coherent worldview, but a loosely assembled emotional landscape.

sections.title: ARTIFICIAL WAVES
sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

In the mimetic domain, they drift passively along oscillatory trajectories, functioning as parametric models. Two conventional beams converge at the system’s periphery, provoking an anomalous, metastable standing wave—its frequency erratic, its amplitude misaligned. Time momentarily arrests at the locus of interference: at a low-probability resonance node, his crest and her trough become phase-inverted, instantaneously cancelling each other through destructive interference, resolving, momentarily, into zero amplitude.

The moon, coarse as a salt crystal, recedes into the damp night—even though its albedo is only 0.12. Within the fishing-light matrix, micro-deviations spiral unchecked—misread by her as another marine body. The surge breaches overhead before the background parameters, persistently amplified, surface as a necessary fault in the perturbation chain. Tolerance thresholds rupture; signs decouple, variables disintegrate, and the algorithm withdraws from its attempt to resolve the state.

Within the shadowed meridian between nautical dusk and dawn, the experimental models survey each other across a shared liminal horizon—engaging in self-preservation routines within data-stream blind spots, continually patching the fractures along the margins of error. In a fleeting moment, the mechanical light of the setting sun etches across the sea’s fault line. He turns and says:

“Perhaps, this time, we needn’t part again.”

sections.title: DROWNING PIANO
sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

YEAR 2020

Thousands upon thousands of instruments chorus across a far, great plain -

until a flying arrow shoots down the silky curtain, carrying it through to the end.

Only I see myself singing, so involuntarily.

Rustling and misting, thousands upon thousands of moths fall into silver ash;

pain like a needle’s spine, life balanced tiptoed on a single-plank bridge.

I’ve been asked to repeatedly practise earthly writing.

I’m changing trousers with my younger self,

like a Christian consuming his own flesh.

乐器成千上万，合唱在大平原。

直至飞矢射落绸幕，有始有终。

只有我看清楚自己身不由己。

瑟瑟复离离，百万蝴蝶的救兵扑落银粉疼成尖针，都要我独木桥上绷起脚尖一样地去活。

我被要求反复练习尘世的书写。

流泪眼，高高叶，热带伤心榕。

我和年轻时候的自己在树下换裤子，就像基督吃了自己的血和肉。

data.notes: In 1954, biologist F.A. Brown moved oysters from Connecticut to a basement aquarium in Chicago. For two weeks, their behaviour was normal. sections.title: CHAOS SYSTEM
sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

The backflow rain disrupted the quantum channels between spacetime continuums, causing echoes of the past to overlap with inorganic projections of the future.

I sincerely invite you to Get Caught in the rain, in the past or future, become quantum entangled with me.

1.      Temporal Chaos

I incorporated steampunk mechanical elements and futuristic transparent materials, treating the entire piece to appear weathered as if it had endured the ravages of war. This approach aligns with the elements of temporal chaos, intentionally blurring the time setting to leave room for audience imagination. The resulting damage and chaos raise the question: was the spark for this destruction ignited in the past, the present, or the future?  

 

2.      Spatial Chaos 

I used the main colours and textures of wasteland aesthetics to shape marine life, fitting the elements of spatial chaos. The natural order of evolution is disrupted by human intervention. If the self-similarity of nature is broken, and the fluid structure of the ocean overlaps with the mountainous formations, does this signify the end of nature.


3.      Temporal Chaos.

The sculpture features remnants of damage, including burn marks and rust, which are traces from the past. Simultaneously, the flowing liquid on the sculpture signifies that it is melting, embodying the coexistence of motion and stillness, aligning with the elements of temporal chaos. Is the apocalyptic catastrophe frozen in yesterday, today, or the present moment?

4.        Functional (or conceptual) Chaos 

While I yearn for the essence of art, my writing and created artworks are burdened with utilitarian motives and complex forms. The content I express is often fragmented, shallow, chaotic, and lacks coherence. There is a significant element of pretentiousness, technical showmanship, and empty posturing. This mirrors the final element of chaos theory: "functional (or conceptual) chaos," reflecting my own turbulent existence in this bizarre and multifaceted space-time. In this state, because of the excessive redundancy of fragmented information, order and chaos coexist, embodying my restless self.

When people genuinely / curiously ask what my work is about, I usually can’t respond shit. I explained “I tore apart a hoover for my cyber jellyfish” back then

For these Ferrari visual materials, I could only start partially meaning-making after the execution

I just realised no matter how fast the Enzo is and how close it seems to entering the city…

The vehicle speeds away rapidly its metaphorical structure is almost like

The individual’s brief resistance to the vast system, or their stubborn pursuit of the distant, prosperous utopian city

sections.title: LAMINA
sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

“Disappear Into Something”

I love how you describe childhood as a form of anarchy - a state where the boundary between people and objects blurs.
When I was little, I had a cat, and I would have long conversations with her.
I truly believed she was an angel traped in white fur.
Insects spoke to me, and I replied.
Tadpoles were twisting black commas, dotting - arranging - a hidden underwater text.
When a tiny bubble surfaced in the pond, I believed it was a message from a frog or fish, finally ready to speak to me.
I still see the world this way - or rather, I like to see the world this way.

When I open my eyes in the morning, I softly greet the ceiling.
Sometimes, when I’m washing dishes, I ask the faucet, “Is the water too hot?”

What matters just as much here is this:
In any artistic practice, one must resist nostalgia for childhood - or the temptation to treat art as an escape from these moments.
Instead, I prefer to see poetry as a space where that childlike, boundaryless perception gets activated in the present moment - both within language and within life - so that we might interact with both at once.

To vanish into something, to become enchanted by it, to let your curiosity overflow, to release the self and let it all happen - that’s a necessary step toward true understanding.
The kind of understanding that shifts how you learn, the way falling in love changes you or how powerful ideas carve lasting marks into that prehistoric part of our brains.
sections.storyChinese:
中文转录

「消失于某物之中」：


我喜欢你对童年作为无政府状态的描绘，一种模糊人与物界限的状态。小时候，我有一只猫，我会和它进行长时间的对话。我坚信它是一只披着白色皮毛的天使。昆虫会对我说话，我也会回应它们。蝌蚪是扭动着的黑色逗号，点缀着、排列着一个潜藏的水下文本。当池塘表面浮起一个小小的气泡时，我认为是青蛙或鱼准备好并送给我的一段话。我至今仍以这种方式看待世界，或者说，我喜欢这样看待世界。


清晨醒来睁开眼睛时，我会轻声向天花板问好。有时在洗碗时，我会问水龙头：水太热了吗？在这里，同样重要的是，在任何艺术实践中都要避免对童年的怀旧，或将艺术视为逃避这些时刻的途径。相反，我更喜欢将诗歌视为一个空间，其中童年那种超出等级或边界的感知力被当下激活，既在语言中，也在生活中，以便同时与语言和生活互动。


消失于某物之中、对其着魔、激发无尽好奇，放下自我、任由这一切发生，是通向真正理解的必要步骤——那种能够改变你的学习方式，如同人生事件如何改变、塑造你（比如坠入爱河），甚至强大观念如何在我们天生无历史感的大脑背后狠狠凿下凹痕。

sections.title: SPRING UNDER THE SKIN
sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

May God visit upon you all that you have visited upon me.

May you live without a consort, and remain unanointed until death.

May you shed tears as you beg for your mother’s milk.

May your bones arch out of the ground.

May your own blood never wash off your agony.

May the serpent bite into the nest of your heart.

May you walk barefoot over a bed of thorns.

May it be my blessing that seals your demise.


This text was sent to me by a friend. Its imagery draws from the Balkan folk tradition of kletve - curses or imprecations - and echoes related passages in Dubravka Ugrešić’s The Ministry of Pain.

愿蛇咬你的心窝。

愿你光脚从荆棘丛上走过。

愿我的祝福杀死你。


这段文字由挚友发给我，其意象源自巴尔干地区的民间 kletve（诅咒）传统，并与 Dubravka Ugrešić 的 The Ministry of Pain 中的相关文本产生呼应。

sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

2011

After the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami, a piano that had been submerged in seawater was recovered. Prolonged exposure to salt water left its metal strings completely rusted, while the wooden keys had swollen with water; many of them, once pressed, could no longer spring back up.

Ryuichi Sakamoto later encountered this “tsunami piano.” Listening to its completely altered sound, he gradually stopped understanding its condition simply as damage or as being out of tune.

“When the pitch is off, people say the piano has loosened, that it has gone out of tune. But perhaps it has not gone out of tune at all. These natural materials are desperately struggling to return to the forms they once had. The waves came rushing in all at once, returning the piano to a state of nature.

Now, I find a piano tuned by nature to be extraordinarily beautiful. Forcing it into tune according to human understanding is unnatural. It may seem natural to us, but from nature’s perspective, it is an unnatural state. I can feel an incredibly strong sense of resistance in that.”

— Ryuichi Sakamoto
sections.storyChinese:
中文转录

2011

2011年东日本大地震与海啸之后，一架被海水淹没的钢琴被发现。长时间的盐水浸泡使金属琴弦完全生锈，木制琴键吸水膨胀，许多琴键按下后再也无法恢复原位。

坂本龙一后来见到了这架“海啸钢琴”。面对它已经完全改变的声音，他逐渐不再把这种状态简单地理解为损坏或走音。

“如果音准不对的话，人们就会说琴松了，走音了。其实并非是走音，而是这些自然的物质正在拼命挣扎，想要回到过去的形态。海浪一瞬间涌上来，让钢琴恢复到自然形态。现在的我觉得经过自然调音的钢琴感觉特别好。人类按照自己的认知强制调音，这是不自然的。虽然对于人类来说是自然，但对于大自然来说，这是不自然的状态。我能感受到非常强烈的对抗感。”

— 坂本龙一

sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

A Reply from a Close Friend:

The world is a peach, and home is its pit. Leaving means risking decay. That pit enshrines an altar of sorrow - an entity steeped in nostalgia. With conflicted resentment, we navigate the labyrinths of opportunity, sometimes forgetting our mother tongue.

The self-devouring identity burrows like a worm, turning accents into performance tools - cultural currency shaped by trauma lodged in our vocal cords. Each linguistic collision becomes a micro-battlefield, an ulcer in the clash between globalization and local identity.

We fail to fully assimilate into urban civilization, yet resist being reabsorbed by our hometowns, patching existential wounds with irony and borrowed superiority - only to watch them seep with the pus of perpetual anxiety.

我们怀着复杂的仇恨，穿越各式各样开云的丛林，甚至有些遗忘我们的母语；身份蠕虫的自我啃噬被作为文化货币的口音成为表演工具，声带里的带痰的创伤记忆，声音场域里每一次对冲留下的微型战场，是全球化与在地性撕扯下的精神溃疡；

我们无法完全消化都市文明的异质养分，又抗拒被小城的文化母体重新收编，于是在系统缝隙中，那些用自嘲与优越感编织的存在主义绷带终究裹不住身份焦虑持续渗出的脓血。”

sections.title: INVERTED BABEL IN ASCENT
sections.storyEnglish:
ENGLISH TRANSMISSION

In the Book of Genesis, humanity once shared a single language. People gathered together and attempted to build a tower whose top would reach the heavens. Their language was later confused, and they could no longer understand one another, so they were scattered across the earth. The Tower of Babel thus became a symbol of fractured language and failed communication.

In Battle Angel Alita, the layers of earth beneath the ground are stacked one above another, arranged from the recent past to increasingly distant ages. The vertical shafts dug to excavate ruins and relics resemble hollow Towers of Babel turned upside down, connecting the underground to the surface, and the old world to the present.

Kaos possesses the ability of psychometry. By touching any object, he can read the object itself, as well as the experiences, memories, emotions, techniques, and other information belonging to those who have also touched it. Psychometry, too, is a hollow vessel, containing immense stretches of memory and history.

When Kaos reaches out and touches the sleeping Gally, a vast amount of information floods into his mind like a river bursting through its banks.

The inverted Tower of Babel allows people to look back on history and move forward from it; the upright Tower of Babel connects Zalem with the ground and allows people to communicate with one another. In a sense, psychometry is itself a form of communication without speech. Yukito Kishiro portrays psychometry as an extraordinarily powerful ability.
sections.storyChinese:
中文转录

《圣经·创世记》中，人类曾拥有同一种语言。他们聚集在一起，试图建造一座高塔，使塔顶通向天空。后来语言被打乱，人们无法再彼此理解，于是四散各地。巴别塔也因此成为语言分裂与沟通失败的象征。


而在《铳梦》中，地下的土层层层叠叠，按照时代从近前到久远鳞次栉比地排列着。挖掘遗迹和遗物的垂直坑洞，就像倒悬着的空心巴别塔，连通地下和地表，沟通着旧时代和现在。


凯奥斯拥有“精神韵律”的能力。接触任何物品，他都能读取该物品，以及同样接触过该物品的人的经历、记忆、情感、技术等等情报。精神韵律也是一个空心的容器，容纳一切漫长悠久的记忆和历史。


当凯奥斯伸手触摸休眠中的加里，如同江河溃堤，大量的信息涌入他的脑海。


倒悬的巴别塔让人们以史为鉴，既往开来；正着的巴别塔让萨雷姆和地面相连，让人们互相沟通。其实，精神韵律也是一种不用说话的沟通。木城五土把精神韵律描绘得很强大。
